 Search The Site President Donald Trump Renews Call To Stop Clocks Changing President Donald Trump Renews Call To Stop Clocks Changing
 Ryan McCredden Ryan McCredden Published: November 11, 2026 Chip Somodevilla, Getty Images Share on Facebook 
 Share on Twitter 
 The sun is going to set today at 4:46 p.m.  The sun will rise again tomorrow at 6:46 a.m.  This is the time of year when Iowa and Illinois will get 10 hours of sun.  And no matter what we do, or don't do, to our clocks, we'll still only get 10 hours of daylight.
 But should that time come in the morning or night?  And most importantly, should that time drastically change twice a year?  There is a new push from President Donald Trump to pass the Sunshine Protection Act, which will keep our clocks the same year-round.
 Does America Want To Change The Clock Twice A Year?
 According to an AP-NORC poll that was published in RadioInk , fifty-six percent want daylight saving time and 42% want permanent standard time. Also, 47% said they oppose the current system of changing clocks twice a year, 40% said they neither favor nor oppose it, and 12% favor it.
 Of course, the country is split pretty much down the middle on what the permanent time should be.  However, take the 40% that don't care either way, and that brings us to 87% of the country would be ok if we stopped changing the clocks twice a year.  There is nothing...and I mean NOTHING...that Americans are in 87% agreement on, except this.
 President Trump Pushes for Sunshine Protection Act
 The House passed the Sunshine Protection Act 308-117 on July 14, but the Senate has not taken it up.  Cause they were busy.  Campaigning.
 The President said, “It’s so dark outside, so early (Sunset was 5:06 P.M., and it was dark by 5:31 P.M. — Isn’t that ridiculous?). Just a few days ago it was so nice and sunny at this same time…I didn’t want to make a big deal out of this prior to the Election because I didn’t want to have certain Senators lose their Race, in a landslide, but it is too bad they can’t get it done.”
 Will this get done before the new group of Senators is sworn in?  If 87% of the population is going to be ok with it passing, then they probably won't.
